_about: Photo-derived materials (CLAUDE.md rule 16). The textures in scripts/v2/materials/<slug>/ are made FROM the owner's photographs with the photo's light divided out; factor x texture (linear) = the base colour on the light-rig scale. Texture coordinates are made at tile build time from position and normal: on a wall u runs along the wall and v up, elsewhere plan x/z; both in metres / repeat_m.

anchor.why: one number to overrule: the build's limestone level is kept; the brick/stone ratio and all colours come from the photograph (overcast, one wall plane, no lamp)

filter.why: measured (v2-shimmer, S 250 m): plain trilinear left the textured wall softer than the truth (+0.02); anisotropy 8 + bias -0.15 gives -0.03 with shimmer 0.00 (main 0.05). The window-frame coverage fade was dropped: it only made the frames softer than the truth (+0.01) and did not lower shimmer.

anchor.why: one number to overrule: the build's limestone level (light rig, stone_value 0.13) is kept; the south block's brick and stone colours come from the owner's IMG_0768 by the build's own rule (photo pixel / the rig's overcast light at the exposure that puts its clean limestone at that level). Only the south block (wall_brick_block) carries the texture; the 1933 pavilion and the wing keep their gated plain colours. The limestone shows no resolvable texture at the photo's 7.5 mm/px (a tile of it repeats a visible blotch), so it is a plain photo-derived colour in the build, not a texture
